mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility fell from 10.4 to 8.0 points in the most recent week, indicating households are spending less time confined at home. This loosening of home-bound behavior should translate into increased discretionary outings, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is not higher than its last-28-day mean despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility rebounded sharply from -49.9 to -40.4 (a 9.5-point jump) in the latest week, signaling renewed outdoor activity and relaxed restrictions. This outdoor-activity rebound typically precedes a broader recovery in retail and recreation footfall within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 8 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to increase within the following two weeks after a PARKS jump exceeding 8 points, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show stabilizing week-on-week changes (WORKPLACES: -25.7 to -26.7, TRANSIT: -27.7 to -27.1), suggesting that commuting and labor-market restrictions are neither tightening nor loosening sharply. When these two series jointly stabilize, retail activity tends to follow a modest upward drift as uncertainty about policy direction fades.
evidence_refs: fact:both series show sub-2-point week-on-week changes over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean declines despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining within 2 points of their prior week values, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-January cold-weather conditions are suppressing outdoor PARKS activity, but this substitution effect pushes discretionary trips toward indoor retail and recreation venues, producing a short-term uptick in RETAIL_REC within one week as consumers shift location type rather than reduce overall mobility.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remains deeply negative (-40.4) relative to RETAIL_REC (-36.7) in the same week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week while PARKS remains substantially below RETAIL_REC's level, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility fell sharply from -9.4 to -17.6 over the prior three weeks before a partial rebound to -13.9, consistent with intermittent restriction tightening around essential-goods access. If GROCERY_PHARM drops below -17 again, it signals renewed restriction tightening that will suppress RETAIL_REC over the following week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -17 points from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM reached -17.6 at t-1w before rebounding to -13.9
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a GROCERY_PHARM drop below -17, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The synchronized dip across RETAIL_REC, PARKS, and GROCERY_PHARM at t-1w (immediately following the New Year holiday period) reflects temporary holiday-driven closures and reduced errands, not a structural decline. As routines normalize post-holiday, RETAIL_REC should recover upward over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:all three series hit local minima at t-1w then partially rebounded at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's mean over the next two weeks does not exceed its t-1w/t-0w average, the post-holiday reversion hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has shown a persistent negative trend over the last three weeks (-25.7, -25.9, -27.7, -27.1), indicating sustained suppression of commuting and errand-related travel. This underlying weakness in transit usage constrains the pool of potential retail visitors, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed or declining over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined roughly 1.4 points net over the four-week window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean rises above its last-28-day mean despite TRANSIT remaining flat or declining, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in PARKS (+9.5 points) and decline in RESIDENTIAL (-2.4 points) in the same week indicates a combined effect of increased outdoor willingness and reduced home confinement. When both shifts occur together, the joint signal produces a stronger and faster short-term boost to RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 9.5 points while RESIDENTIAL fell 2.4 points in the same week (t-0w)
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week when PARKS rises and RESIDENTIAL falls concurrently, the interaction hypothesis is falsified.
